tictactoe.intro: Take turns placing your mark on the 3×3 board.

sections.title: How to win
items: Get three of your marks in a row — across, down or diagonally.
If the board fills up with no line, it's a draw.

avalon.intro: The agents try to complete three operations. Moles hide among them and try to make three operations fail.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: A team game of hidden identities. Agents try to complete operations; moles hide among them and sabotage.
items: Each player is secretly an Agent or a Mole. Moles know each other; most agents know nobody.
The game lasts up to five operations. Agents need three to succeed; moles need three to fail.
Agents who reach three successes still have to survive the Hitman's guess at the Handler.
Moles also win if five proposed teams in a row are rejected.
Roles are dealt at random and depend on the number of players (see Setup).

round.title: Each round
items: Leader: the player with the crown proposes a team of the size shown on the track.
Vote: everyone approves or rejects. Votes are revealed together once all are in.
A strict majority approves the team. A tie is a rejection.
Rejected: the crown passes to the next player, who proposes a new team. Five rejections in a row and the moles win.
Approved: each team member secretly plays Success or Fail — hold the card for 2 seconds. Agents can only play Success; moles may play either.
The cards are revealed without names. One Fail fails the operation (Operation 4 needs two with 7 or more players).
The crown moves on and the next operation begins.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Eight roles in total. Which ones are in a game depends on the player count — see Setup.

setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Roles in play and team size for each of the five operations, by number of players.

ending.title: The ending
items: Three failed operations: the moles win at once.
Three successful operations: the moles are revealed and may talk it over. The Hitman then names one agent as the Handler.
If the Hitman is right, the moles steal the win. If wrong, the agents win.
When the game ends, everyone's role is shown.

more.title: More rules
items: Discussion happens out loud. Anyone may lie about anything — but never show your screen.
Your role card is face down until you tap it. Tap again to hide it.
Team votes are public once revealed and stay in History. Operation cards are never linked to a player — only the number of Fails is shown.
Handler: hint, don't announce. The more obvious you are, the easier the Hitman's job.
A mole on a team doesn't have to play Fail. Playing Success can build trust.
If a player leaves mid-game, the game ends for everyone and all roles are revealed.

merlin.note: Stay hidden. If the agents win three operations, the Hitman wins the game by naming you.

percival.knows: Who the Handler and the Decoy are — but not which is which.
percival.note: Work out the real Handler and shield them.

assassin.knows: The other moles, except the Wildcard.
assassin.note: If the agents win three operations, you name one agent as the Handler. Guess right and the moles win.

morgana.knows: The other moles, except the Wildcard.
morgana.note: The Bodyguard sees you as a possible Handler.

mordred.knows: The other moles, except the Wildcard.

oberon.knows: Nothing — and the other moles don't know you either.

minion.knows: The other moles, except the Wildcard.

labels.twoFails: * This operation needs two Fail cards to fail.

coup.intro: Everyone runs two stalls — two hidden cards. Bluff, challenge and block until you are the last player with a card left. The deck has 15 cards: 3 each of Boss, Enforcer, Pickpocket, Fixer and Auntie.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Everyone runs a crew of two hidden cards. Bluff, challenge and block until you're the last player with a card left.
items: Setup: each player gets 2 face-down cards and $2. The deck has 15 cards — 3 each of Boss, Enforcer, Pickpocket, Fixer and Auntie.
On your turn you take exactly one action. Some actions need a role — but you may claim a role you don't have.
After you announce an action, the other players may challenge your claim or block the action.
A card you lose is turned face up. Lose both and you're out.
The last player with a card wins.
Everyone's cash and lost cards are public. Face-down cards and the deck are secret.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Five roles, three copies of each. A role gives you a special action, lets you block something, or both.

actions.title: Actions
actions.intro: Take one per turn. "Needs" is the role you must claim — truthfully or not.

challenges.title: Challenges
items: Whenever a player claims a role — to take an action or to block one — any other player may challenge.
Everyone else chooses Challenge or Allow. The first challenge settles it.
If it was a bluff: the bluffer loses a card. A bluffed action doesn't happen; a bluffed block fails and the action goes through.
If it was true: the challenger loses a card. The proven card is shuffled back into the deck and replaced with a new one, so the hand stays secret.
Day Job, Borrow and Shut Down claim no role, so they can't be challenged.
Once you tap Allow, you can't challenge that claim any more.

blocks.title: Blocks
items: Borrow can be blocked by any player claiming Boss.
Pickpocket can be blocked only by its target, claiming Pickpocket or Fixer.
Rough Up can be blocked only by its target, claiming Auntie.
A block is a claim, so anyone may challenge it. If the block was a bluff, the blocker loses a card and the action still happens.
A successful block cancels the action. Money already paid is not returned.
Day Job, Collect Rent, Swap and Shut Down can't be blocked.

more.title: More rules
items: With $10 or more at the start of your turn, you must Shut Down someone.
Rough Up costs $3 up front. You get it back only if you're caught bluffing the Enforcer — not if the action is blocked.
Double loss: bluff Auntie against a Rough Up and get challenged, and you lose one card for the bluff and one for the Rough Up.
With two cards, you choose which one to lose. With one card left there's no choice.
When you're out, your cash is gone and you only watch.
Two players: whoever goes first starts with $1 instead of $2.
If a player leaves mid-game, the game ends for everyone with no winner.
Tap your cards to flip them face down when someone might peek.

effects.steal: Take $2 from another player (or whatever they have, if less).
effects.exchange: Draw 2 cards from the deck, then return any 2. Changes your roles in secret.
effects.assassinate: Choose a player; they lose a card.
effects.coup: Choose a player; they lose a card. Nothing can stop it.

labels.anyone: No role — anyone can do it

manor.intro: A rich old man has his relatives over for the night. Some are intruders in disguise who want him dead before dawn. The rest must keep him alive until 6 AM.

sections.title: Sides
items: Household: the Butler, the Guard and the Guests. Intruders: 1 with 4 players, 2 with 5–6, 3 with 7–8.
Intruders know each other. The Butler always knows where the old man was at the start of each hour. The Guard carries the flashlight.
With 4 players, the lone intruder starts holding the knife.

sections.title: Each hour
items: The night runs from 10 PM to 6 AM: 8 hours. Everyone starts in the Grand Hall; the old man starts in the Bedroom.
Move: secretly stay, or go one room up, down, left or right. Intruders can slip into any room. Nobody can stay in the Security Room two hours in a row.
Act: Secretly pick one action. It's dark — you know whether someone else is in your room and whether the old man is there, but not who, how many, or what they do.

sections.title: Actions
items: Guard: protect the old man. Attack (intruders with a weapon): hurts him if attackers outnumber guards.
Take a weapon: the knife (Kitchen), candlestick (Library) or poison (Wine Cellar). You carry one item; taking another swaps it.
Fix a camera (Library, Bedroom, Kitchen, Foyer, Garden); intruders can break one. You only see whether a camera is on from its own room or from the Security Room — nobody is told when it changes.
Watch the monitors (Security Room): see who working cameras saw this hour and whether the old man came or went — not what anyone did.
Search: pat down someone at random — you only learn whether they carry something. The Guard learns who it was and what they carry.
Flashlight (Guard): see who is in your room and what each of them does this hour. Escort: the old man follows you next hour.
Once a game, an intruder can hide their weapon for an hour: searches find nothing on them.

sections.title: Meetings
items: After midnight, after 3 AM and after every scream, the household talks it over and votes.
A majority locks a player up for the rest of the night. Their role stays secret.

sections.title: How it ends
items: Intruders win if the old man is hit twice. The first hit makes him scream — everyone learns the room, not who.
The household wins if every intruder is locked up, or the old man is alive at dawn.
At dawn the intruders get one last chance: their ringleader names the Butler. Get it right and the intruders win.

liarsdice.intro: The bar classic. Everyone shakes 5 dice and looks only at their own. Take turns bidding how many of one face are on the whole table — until someone calls a lie.

sections.title: Bidding
items: A bid is "N × face": at least N dice on the table show that face, counting everyone's dice.
The opening bid must be more than the number of players (2 players: at least 3).
Each bid must be higher: more dice, or the same number of a higher face. Faces rank 2 < 3 < 4 < 5 < 6 < 1.
Scattered (散骰): if your five dice all show different faces, you may show them to the table and shake again — any time before your first bid of the round.

sections.title: Wild 1s and zhai
items: The opening bid picks the round: zhai (斋) — 1s count only as 1s — or kaizhai (开斋) — 1s are wild and count as any face. Calling 1s is always zhai.

A zhai round can break the fast (开斋, also called 飞): 1s become wild again, but you must call at least double the dice (after 3 × 4 zhai, at least 6). An opening zhai bid may be as low as the number of players.
Once a round is kaizhai it stays kaizhai: nobody can go back to zhai, so nobody can call 1s.
Five of a kind (豹子): a cup whose five dice all count for the bid counts as six. With wild 1s, two 1s + three 3s are six 3s; under zhai they're just three 3s, while five real 3s still count as six.

sections.title: Calling a lie
items: Open (开): on your turn, instead of bidding, call the last bid a lie. Everyone's dice are revealed and counted. If there are enough, the caller drinks 1 cup; if not, the bidder does.
Split (劈): anyone — not just the player up — can split the last bid at any time. The loser drinks 2 cups.
Counter-split (反劈): the player who was split can counter. Then the loser drinks 4.

sections.title: Winning
items: After each call everyone still in shakes again, and the loser starts the next round.
Knockout: 5 cups and you're drunk — out. The last player standing wins.
Endless: nobody is ever out; cups just add up. When more than half the table votes to stop, the fewest cups win.
The host picks the mode in the lobby.

nightwatch.intro: The manor is haunted. Over five nights the watchers must light the seal lamp to lock the ghosts away — but some of them are possessed and quietly make the seal fail.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Eight roles. Which ones are in a game depends on the number of players. Evil players know each other, and the evil player in the lowest seat is also the assassin.

sections.title: Sides
items: Good: Prophet, Apprentice, Tracker, Keeper (6+), Watchers (8+). Evil: Double, Hermit, Possessed (7+, two with 10).
Evil players know each other. The evil player in the lowest seat is also the assassin.
Prophet: knows who is evil, except the Hermit. Apprentice: sees the Prophet and the Double, but not which is which.

Tracker (twice a game): on the patrol, follow a player to the room they really reach, however far. Keeper (once a game): before the patrol, lock one door for the night — only the door is announced, never who locked it.

Double (twice a game): on the patrol, pick a real room and a decoy room, both ones you could reach. People in the decoy's room see you; in the real room nobody does, but you still use its function there. The decoy counts as a person in its room, but not for the Garden; the Kitchen hears the decoy's room; in the Dining Room the decoy passes for good.

sections.title: The house
items: 3×3 rooms: Bell Tower, Study, Chapel / Gallery, Hall, Dining Room / Cellar, Kitchen, Garden. You move up, down, left or right — never diagonally.
Everyone starts in the Hall. Where you are is secret: after moving you only see who shares your room. Where others are is only what they tell you.
Each night's mission room is drawn at random — never the Hall, never the same room twice in a row. The next night's room is announced a night early.

sections.title: Each night
items: Announcement: tonight's mission room and team size, the next night's room, and from night 2 a night event.
Patrol (secret, all at once): stay, or walk one room. Then you see who is in your room.

Rooms: use your room's function. It doesn't work in tonight's mission room or the Hall, or in a room whose function you used last night (being sent on a mission or moved to the Hall doesn't count as using it).
Discussion: anonymous letters are shown first. Then talk — lying is allowed.

Team: the leader (by seat; the Bell Tower cuts in) names exactly the team size. Everyone votes in public; more than half approves. Otherwise the next leader tries, with no new patrol. Five rejected teams in one night and evil wins.

Mission: the team walks to the mission room — two rooms at most (secret doors and the Cellar passage count). If anyone can't make it, the mission fails at once and the app names who didn't arrive. Otherwise each plays Success or Fail in secret (good can only play Success); only the number of fails is shown.
One fail card fails a mission — except the 4th mission with 7 or more players, which needs two. The team stays in the mission room; the next patrol starts from where everyone is.

sections.title: How it ends
items: Evil wins with three failed missions, or five rejected teams in one night.
When three missions succeed, evil is revealed and may talk it over; the assassin then names the Prophet. Right, and evil wins. Wrong, and good wins.

rooms.intro: After the patrol you use the function of the room you're in. A room that needs an exact number of people won't work with any other number. Tonight's mission room and the Hall have no function, and a room's function can't be used two rounds running (going on a mission or being moved to the Hall doesn't count as using it).
rooms.belltower: Ring the bell: you lead this round (you cut in, then the order carries on).
rooms.study: Read the record: pick one of last night's team and learn whether they played success or fail.
rooms.chapel: Pray: tonight's mission loses one fail card. It works once a game, and isn't used up if there was no fail to take back. Only those in the Chapel that night learn whether it worked. Anyone who enters later can open the book on the lectern: whether anyone prayed on each past night and what came of it (not who).
rooms.gallery: Anonymous letter: write one sentence, shown when discussion starts with no name on it.
rooms.hall: Crossroads: no function, but it's one step from four rooms.
rooms.dining: Share a drink: the two of you each learn the other's side.
rooms.cellar: Secret passage: if you're named for tonight's mission you reach the mission room from here at any distance; if not, next patrol you can go to any room.
rooms.kitchen: Eavesdrop: pick a player and learn which room they ended up in after this patrol.
rooms.garden: Lookout: learn how many people are in each room this round (not who).

events.intro: From night 2, one night event is flipped at each announcement, for everyone to see.
events.blackout: After this patrol you can't see who shares your room — only whether anyone does.
events.collapse: A random room is sealed for good: nobody can enter it again, and anyone inside is moved to the Hall. It is never tonight's or the next night's mission room.
events.secretDoor: Two random diagonal rooms are joined for good: you can walk straight between them.
events.storm: Nobody can move on this patrol, and the Tracker can't follow anyone.
events.insomnia: Everyone may walk up to two rooms on this patrol.
events.echo: The Gallery may post two anonymous letters this round.
events.fog: The team can only walk one room to the mission this round, not two.

counts.title: Player counts
counts.intro: 5 to 10 players. The count sets how many are good and evil, which roles are dealt, and how big each night's team is:
counts.star: * This night's mission needs 2 Fail cards to fail.

items: N1–N5: how many go on that night's mission; the leader names exactly that many.
Votes: approvals a team needs to set out (more than half the table).
Five teams rejected in a row on one night and evil wins, at any count.
The evil player in the lowest seat is also the assassin, who names the Prophet if three missions succeed.

shelter.intro: Winter has come and the town is gone. You've barricaded yourselves into an old house and must last 6 days until the rescue convoy arrives. Everyone starts on the same side — but on the 2nd or 3rd night the sickness takes one of you. From then on they want the shelter to starve, and nobody knows who it is.

items: Day: everyone at a place plays one card face down; they're shuffled and turned over. The Infected can slip in Sabotage −2 — everyone sees it, nobody knows whose.
Night: everyone secretly guards the storeroom, guards the door or sleeps; the Infected at the same time steals, opens the door or sleeps. Meet a guard and you're seen; miss them and it works.
Morning: only a guard saw the Infected. When they say so, everyone has to decide whether to believe them.
Guards are tired the next day and draw 1 card — the harder you guard, the less food you find.
clashes.0: Day: everyone at a place plays one card face down; they're shuffled and turned over. The Infected can play a Mould −2 that looks exactly like the real mould in the decks — nobody can tell bad luck from sabotage.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Everyone starts as a Survivor. The Infected turns in secret partway through.
survivor: Goal: last until the rescue on day 6, or send every Infected out.
By day, scavenge; at night, guard the storeroom, guard the door or sleep.
Guarding where the Infected strikes shows you who it is.
infected: On the 2nd or 3rd night a random Survivor is infected (with 6+, a second one two nights later).
Goal: empty the storeroom, make Survivors fall, or leave too few standing when the rescue comes.
By day you can play Mould (sabotage) −2, which turns over as ordinary mould; at night steal a third of the storeroom (at least 2) or open the door to a zombie.
With 5 players the Infected can Sneak once: that night they succeed even if guarded, unseen.
Two Infected don't know each other.

places.title: Places & posts
places.intro: By day everyone secretly picks a place, draws 2 cards (1 when tired or weak) and plays 1 face down. Cards are drawn at random from the decks below.
places.farm: The steady place: mostly food, but some come back empty or mouldy.
places.market: The most food, but plenty of it rots, and zombies roam. Anyone bitten can't go out the next day.
places.hospital: Medicine: at dawn, each one treats an injured or weak player.

posts.title: The three posts at night
posts.intro: At night everyone secretly taps one spot in the house. The Infected sees the same three spots, meaning something else.

store.survivor: Guard the storeroom: if someone comes to steal, you see who. One guard to a post — the first to choose it; anyone later goes back to bed. Tired tomorrow.
store.infected: Steal: if nobody guards it, take a third of the storeroom (at least 2) and eat it. The fuller the storeroom, the more you take.

door.survivor: Guard the door: if someone comes to open it, you see who. One guard to a post. Tired tomorrow.
door.infected: Open the door: if nobody guards it, a zombie gets in, the storeroom loses 1 and a sleeper is hurt.

sleep.survivor: Sleep: rest, and draw 2 cards tomorrow.
sleep.infected: Pretend to sleep: do nothing, and can't be seen.

flow.title: Each day
items: Morning (after the first cough): talk about the night, then vote. More than half of those standing on one name sends them out, and their role is shown.
Day: everyone secretly picks a place (farm, market, and the hospital with 5+). The injured stay home.
Cards: draw 2, play 1 face down. Cards at one place are shuffled and turned over; their total goes into the storeroom.
Night: everyone secretly taps the storeroom, the door or a bed. One guard to a post (the first to choose it). The Infected succeeds where nobody guards; meeting a guard fails and gets them seen.
Supper: everyone standing eats 1 from the storeroom. Short? Someone goes hungry: one night weak (1 card tomorrow), two nights running and they fall.
The fallen can do nothing but watch.
At the start of the 2nd or 3rd night the app announces a cough. With 6+, a second cough comes two nights later.

counts.title: Player counts
counts.intro: 4 to 8 players. The count sets the number of Infected, the starting food and the win thresholds:

items: Rescue needs: Survivors still standing after supper on night 6.
Famine at: if the storeroom runs out and this many go hungry, the Infected win.
Votes: needed with everyone standing. It drops as people fall or are sent out (always more than half of those standing).
5 players: the hospital opens and the Infected can Sneak once.
6–8 players: 2 Infected; the second turns two nights after the first, and they don't know each other. Both must be sent out to win that way.

winning.title: Winning
items: Survivors win: after supper on night 6, at least the 'rescue needs' number are standing; or every Infected has been sent out.
The Infected win: the storeroom runs out and the 'famine at' number go hungry.
The Infected win: at any time, Survivors standing are no more than Infected standing.
The Infected win: when the rescue comes, too few Survivors are standing.
Sending out a Survivor doesn't end the game: one fewer to scavenge, but one fewer mouth too.

liarsdice.breakZhai: Break the fast (开斋) — 1s wild again

revealBy.counter: {{name}} split the {{bid}} call by {{bidder}} — who countered!

liarsdice.lockedKaizhai: This round is kaizhai: 1s are wild, and nobody can call zhai or 1s.

nightwatch.tagline: Light the seal before the ghosts break free

fns.belltower: Ring the bell — needs exactly 1 person. You're alone here, so you lead this round.
fns.study: Read the record — needs exactly 1 person. You're alone here: see the card one of last night's team played.
fns.chapel: Pray: tonight's mission loses one fail card. It works once a game.
fns.gallery: Write an anonymous letter, shown to everyone when discussion starts.
fns.hall: No function — but it's one step from four rooms.
fns.dining: Share a drink — needs exactly 2 people. There are exactly two of you here, so you each learn the other's side.
fns.cellar: Secret passage: on the team, you reach the mission room from here; if not, next patrol you can go anywhere.
fns.kitchen: Eavesdrop: learn which room one player ended up in.
fns.garden: Lookout: you see how many people are in each room.

prophet.name: Prophet
prophet.desc: Good. You know who is evil — except the Hermit. Guide the others quietly: if three missions succeed, the assassin hunts you.

apprentice.name: Apprentice
apprentice.desc: Good. You saw two people: one is the Prophet, the other the Double — you can't tell which.

tracker.name: Tracker
tracker.desc: Good. Twice a game, on the patrol, follow a player: you end up in whatever room they really reach, however far.

keeper.name: Keeper
keeper.desc: Good. Once a game, before the patrol, lock one door for the night — nobody passes through it on the patrol or the mission. Everyone hears which door, never who locked it.

watcher.name: Watcher
watcher.desc: Good. No special power: patrol, listen, and light the seal.

double.name: Double
double.desc: Evil. Twice a game, on the patrol, leave a decoy in another room you could reach. People there see you; in your real room nobody does. The Apprentice sees you as a possible Prophet.

hermit.name: Hermit
hermit.desc: Evil. The Prophet can't see you.

blackout.name: Blackout
blackout.desc: After the patrol you can't see who shares your room — only whether anyone does.

collapse.name: Collapse
collapse.desc: A room caved in for good: nobody can enter it, and anyone inside was moved to the Hall.

secretDoor.name: Secret door
secretDoor.desc: Two diagonal rooms are now joined for good.

storm.name: Storm
storm.desc: Nobody can move on this patrol, and the Tracker can't follow anyone.

insomnia.name: Insomnia
insomnia.desc: Everyone may walk up to two rooms on this patrol.

echo.name: Echo
echo.desc: The Gallery may post two letters tonight.

fog.name: Fog
fog.desc: The team can only walk one room to the mission tonight, not two.

bar.trackHint: Team size each night · ★ needs two fail cards

role.title: Your role
role.knowsProphet: One of these is the Prophet, the other the Double: {{names}}
role.assassin: {{name}} is the assassin and names the Prophet at the end
role.youAssassin: You are the assassin: you name the Prophet at the end

announce.title: Tonight
announce.twoFails: This mission needs two fail cards to fail
announce.noEvent: No night event on the first night.

map.notesHint: Pick a watcher, then tap the room you think they were in that night. Only you see this.

prompt.readyHint: Read tonight's mission and event, then tap ready.
prompt.lockHint: Once a game. Everyone hears which door — never who locked it.
prompt.patrolHint: Stay, or walk to a room next door. You can also tap the map.
prompt.patrolStorm: The storm keeps everyone where they are.
prompt.patrolFree: The Cellar's passage is open: go to any room.
prompt.patrolInsomnia: Insomnia: walk up to two rooms.
prompt.followHint: You end up wherever they really are. {{count}} left.
prompt.decoyHint: People in the decoy's room see you; in your real room nobody does. {{count}} left.
prompt.noFn: This room does nothing for you tonight.
prompt.letterHint: No name is shown. Leave it blank to skip.
prompt.prayHint: If tonight's mission has a fail card, one is taken back. Only those in the Chapel learn whether it worked. It works once a game.
prompt.proposeHint: Talk it over first. Anyone more than {{steps}} room(s) from the {{room}} won't make it — and the mission fails.
prompt.missionHintEvil: Play Success or Fail. Only the number of fail cards is revealed.
prompt.assassinateHint: Talk it over with your side first. Name the Prophet and evil wins.
prompt.name: Name them

waiting.team: {{name}} is choosing a team — talk it over!
waiting.mission: The team is on the mission…

where.someone: Someone is here — too dark to see who

blocked.mission: Tonight's mission room has no function.
blocked.repeat: You used this room last night — no function tonight.

where.onMission: You were sent on the mission and have walked into the {{room}}. You stay here afterwards: next night's patrol starts from this room.
where.afterMission: You went on last night's mission, so you are still in the {{room}}. Tonight's patrol starts from here.

notes.bell: You rang the bell: you lead this round
notes.cellar: The passage is open: on the team you reach the mission from here; otherwise any room next patrol

prayer.none: No fail card was taken back
prayer.noCards: No cards were played — the prayer wasn't needed

notes.collapse: The {{room}} caved in — you were moved to the Hall

records.cancelled: a prayer took back a fail card

records.noCards: a prayer, but no cards were played

log.title: Your notebook
log.hint: Only you can see this. Share it — or lie.

reasons.assassination: Three missions succeeded, but the assassin found the Prophet: {{prophet}}.

knockout.name: Knockout
knockout.desc: 5 cups and you're out. Last one standing wins.

endless.name: Endless
endless.desc: Nobody's out — just keep drinking. Vote to stop; fewest cups wins.

shelter.tagline: Last six winter days — but someone turns in the night

cardHints.medicine: At dawn, treats one injured or weak player
cardHints.sabotage: Infected only: 2 less, and it turns over exactly like real mould

news.title: What happened
news.zombieHurt: {{names}} got bitten and stays home tomorrow
news.cough: Someone is coughing in the dark…
news.opened: The door was opened and a zombie got in
news.injured: {{names}} got hurt and stays home tomorrow

notes.caught: You were seen: {{names}} stood guard there
notes.stoleSneaked: You sneaked in and stole {{count}} food unseen
notes.openedSneaked: You sneaked to the door and opened it unseen
notes.bumped: Someone was already guarding the {{post}}, so you went back to bed (not tired tomorrow)

cough.title: Someone is coughing in the dark…
cough.body: Someone is infected. From tonight, they want the shelter to starve.
cough.youBody: From now on you are the Infected. By day you can play Mould (sabotage), which looks just like real mould; at night you can steal food or open the door — don't get seen.

task.fallen: You collapsed from hunger and can only watch now.
task.exiled: You were sent out of the shelter and can only watch now.
task.injured: You're hurt and stay home today.
task.voteHint: {{count}} votes send someone out. Their role is shown.
task.tired: You stood guard last night: you draw only 1 card today.
task.play: At the {{place}}: play one card face down
task.playHint: Cards at the same place are shuffled and turned over: everyone sees what came up, not who played it.
task.night: Where do you keep watch tonight?
task.nightHint: Tap the storeroom, the door or a bed. A guard sees anyone who comes to do harm, but is tired tomorrow.
task.nightInfectedHint: Tap the storeroom to steal, the door to open it, or a bed to pretend to sleep. If someone guards it, you'll be seen.

reasons.rescue: They made it to day 6 and the convoy arrived.
reasons.exiled: Every Infected was sent out of the shelter.
reasons.famine: The storeroom ran empty and too many went hungry.
reasons.outnumbered: The Infected standing were no fewer than the Survivors.
reasons.lateRescue: The convoy came, but too few Survivors were still standing.
